content.text: Search logs show `results_count=0` for about half of requests, and rate logs show many `hotel_count=0`. I'll compare these against the normal period.

input.query: SELECT 'ab' p, service_name, regexp_extract(message,'(results_count|hotel_count)=[0-9]+',0) k, count(*) n FROM abnormal_logs WHERE service_name IN ('search','rate') GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'no', service_name, regexp_extract(message,'(results_count|hotel_count)=[0-9]+',0), count(*) FROM normal_logs WHERE service_name IN ('search','rate') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text: The `results_count` and `hotel_count` ratios match normal, so those are not a fault signal. I'll look at the HTTP attributes and time profile of the search→rate client spans, normal versus abnormal.

input.query: SELECT 'ab' p, service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind k, attr_status_code sc, attr_http_response_status_code code, avg(attr_http_request_content_length) reqlen, avg(attr_http_response_content_length) resp, count(*) n, approx_quantile(duration/1e6,0.5) p50 FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name IN ('search','rate') GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'no', service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind, attr_status_code, attr_http_response_status_code, avg(attr_http_request_content_length), avg(attr_http_response_content_length), count(*), approx_quantile(duration/1e6,0.5) FROM normal_traces WHERE service_name IN ('search','rate') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 3,4,1

content.text: The rate server spans stay fast while the search client spans take about 2.2 s. To place the gap, I'll join client and server spans by trace and parent ID and measure the time before the server starts and after it ends.

input.query: WITH c AS (SELECT trace_id, span_id, duration d, epoch_ms(time) t FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='search' AND span_name='rate.Rate/GetRates' AND attr_span_kind='Client'), s AS (SELECT trace_id, parent_span_id, duration d, epoch_ms(time) t FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='rate' AND span_name='rate.Rate/GetRates' AND attr_span_kind='Server') SELECT count(*) n, approx_quantile((s.t-c.t),0.5) start_gap_ms_p50, approx_quantile((c.t+c.d/1e6)-(s.t+s.d/1e6),0.5) end_gap_ms_p50, approx_quantile(c.d/1e6,0.5) client_ms, approx_quantile(s.d/1e6,0.5) server_ms FROM c JOIN s ON c.trace_id=s.trace_id AND c.span_id=s.parent_span_id

content.text: Only 17 client/server pairs joined, but the median gap is about 1.9 s before the server starts and about 0.17 s after it ends, so the delay sits mostly on the request leg. I'll look at the duration distribution of search→rate calls to see whether every call is affected or only a fraction.

input.query: SELECT 'ab' p, count(*) n, approx_quantile(duration/1e6,0.05) p05, approx_quantile(duration/1e6,0.25) p25, approx_quantile(duration/1e6,0.5) p50, approx_quantile(duration/1e6,0.75) p75, approx_quantile(duration/1e6,0.95) p95, min(duration/1e6) mn, max(duration/1e6) mx, sum(case when duration>1e9 then 1 else 0 end) over1s FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='search' AND span_name='rate.Rate/GetRates' AND attr_span_kind='Client' UNION ALL SELECT 'no', count(*), approx_quantile(duration/1e6,0.05), approx_quantile(duration/1e6,0.25), approx_quantile(duration/1e6,0.5), approx_quantile(duration/1e6,0.75), approx_quantile(duration/1e6,0.95), min(duration/1e6), max(duration/1e6), sum(case when duration>1e9 then 1 else 0 end) FROM normal_traces WHERE service_name='search' AND span_name='rate.Rate/GetRates' AND attr_span_kind='Client'

content.text: About 94% of search→rate calls take 1.9–2.5 s, against under 1 ms normally, so this is a connection-wide added delay rather than an intermittent one. I'll pull the normal-versus-abnormal user-facing numbers to back the propagation chain.
